exercisePrompt: In the game you played {{move}}. Find a better option: look for checks, captures, and threats, then your opponent’s strongest reply.
poolHint: Extended bank — best move from deep analysis; full line only on core exercises.
optionsTitle: Before you decide, review your options
boardExplainer: You do not need to type moves. Select them on the board and MoveMirror will write the notation for you.
checksQuestion: Did you find a move that gives check?
threatsQuestion: Did you find a move that creates a threat?
noChecks: I did not see a check
noCaptures: I did not see a capture
noThreats: I did not see a threat
threatNote: What would this move try to achieve? — optional
candidateHint: Choose a move you considered or select another legal move on the board.
replyTitle: If you play {{move}}, what would be your opponent’s strongest reply?
replyHint: Play the reply that would make you most uncomfortable on the board.
noneFoundRecorded: You indicated that you could not find a reply.
checkmateEnds: The game ends with this move.
keepQuestion: After looking at your opponent’s reply, do you keep your move?
missingChecks: Indicate whether you saw a check.
missingCaptures: Indicate whether you saw a capture.
missingThreats: Indicate whether you saw a threat.
missingCandidate: Choose the move you would play.
missingReply: Select an opponent reply or indicate that you could not find one.
illegalMove: That move is not legal in this position.

select.checks: Select a checking move on the board.
select.captures: Select a capture on the board.
select.threats: Select a move that creates a threat on the board.
select.candidate: Select the move you would play on the board.
select.reply: Select your opponent’s reply on the board.

notationAuto: MoveMirror writes the moves for you.
notationPieces: K = king · Q = queen · R = rook · B = bishop · N = knight. Pawns have no letter.
notationSymbols: x = capture · + = check · # = checkmate · O-O = kingside castle · O-O-O = queenside castle
notationExamples: Examples: e4 — the pawn moves to e4 · Nf3 — the knight moves to f3 · Bxf2+ — the bishop captures on f2 with check
notationInternational: Saved notation uses the international piece letters in every interface language.
opponentReplyLabel: If you play that, what is your opponent’s strongest reply?
yourMoveHint: Move a piece legally or type a move:
reasonPlaceholder: Why did you choose this move? Did you check your opponent’s strongest reply?
noSolutionYet: You will not see the official solution yet.
unverifiedWarn: The move is legal, but we have not verified it yet.
reflectionVerified: What check of your opponent convinced you your candidate was safe?
reflectionBeforeMove: Before you played, did you consider {{hint}}?
reflectionHintCapture: this capture or recapture from your opponent ({{reply}})
reflectionHintForced: the most awkward forced capture or check from your opponent
